kf1.tip: Imagine a cell skips DNA replication in interphase and goes straight into mitosis. Say what each of the two daughter cells would end up with, and why.
kf1.note: A strong answer starts from the lesson's point that interphase copies the DNA so each daughter cell can get a full set of chromosomes, 46 in humans. With no copying, there is only one set to share out. Each daughter cell would get fewer than 46 chromosomes and miss some DNA. The trap is saying both cells would still be normal and genetically identical to the parent. That only works because the DNA was replicated first.

kf2.tip: Predict whether diffusion speeds up or slows down if you raise the temperature, shrink the surface area, then increase the distance, giving the reason for each.
kf2.note: Raising the temperature speeds diffusion up, because the particles gain more kinetic energy and move faster. Shrinking the surface area slows it down, because there is less membrane for particles to cross. Increasing the distance also slows it down, because the particles have further to travel. If you only wrote faster or slower without a reason, add the reason to each one.

dg1.tip: Sketch a cell membrane from memory with one arrow each for diffusion, osmosis and active transport, labelling the direction of each and which need energy.
dg1.note: Check your sketch against this. Your diffusion arrow should run from high to low concentration. Your osmosis arrow should show water crossing a partially permeable membrane, from the dilute solution to the more concentrated one. Your active transport arrow should go the other way, from low to high concentration. Only active transport should be labelled as needing energy, which comes from respiration in the mitochondria. Diffusion and osmosis should be labelled passive.

cs1.tip: Make the strongest case for and against using embryonic stem cells to treat paralysis or diabetes, then decide which side wins and say why in one line.
cs1.note: A strong case for says embryonic stem cells can become almost any cell type, while adult stem cells from bone marrow are more limited. That makes them more useful for treating paralysis or diabetes. The case against is the ethical objection to using embryos. Most decide the medical benefit wins, though either side can win if your one line is justified. The trap is arguing only one side, or naming ethics vaguely and never weighing it against the benefit.
